frog.speaker: F
frog.excerpt: When we left Tehran, we were looking for a campsite, then Dad saw a road.  We went on a bit, there was a sign with a crown on! And a speed limit saying 40 miles an hour.  Then there was a bridge and a corner suddenly Dad saw a fox, we gave it a chase then it turned off the road.  We found a place to camp then we went exploring.  Helena and I found a big man-made rectangular pond with two pipes in making a waterfall.  The pipes let to a small ordinary pool with lots of frogs in.  It disappeared under a bush.

frog.speaker: H
frog.excerpt: We camped near Tehran by a leading off(?) road.  Francis and I discovered a pond with lots of frogs in it.  When driving, we chased a fox on the road then he ran off.  There was one adventurous frog and one frog who stayed in one place under our spot light (coming from the torch).  The frogs were a sandy colour with splodges of brown, green or greenish brown on them.  We went into a coal mine and saw all the pit props.  We have arrived at the Caspian Sea.  There is lots of greenery compared with the rest of Iran.  Some bits are like England.  F and I built a pyramid with a very small city.  There was one farm, a store house, a cafe and a place where the soldiers live in (a Barock ) and a huge pyramid.

frog.speaker: D
frog.excerpt: Two other vans came and parked by us, they were German, we made another fire, and talked with them, they had beer, but they gave me some Pepsi Cola.  (F&H were in bed.)  We woke up quite early, and were away before the Germans were awake.  We passed a dead badger by the side of the road.  We drove for a long time, we were hoping to reach the forest, to camp in, by nightfall, on the way we made a small detour to see a pencil-like monument.  It was someone’s tomb, and was over 900 years old.  We did in fact reach the forest and camped by the road, but when we were all in bed a warden came and told us (very nicely) to come somewhere else where it was better (he said).  There were lots of frogs.

frog.speaker: H
frog.excerpt: Golegosten Park.  Francis, Dad, Denise, Mum and I had lunch.  Dad made a fire in a metal thing with holes in the bottom and sides and half of it was strips of metal forming a grill.  We fried four small bananas, eight slices of ham, roasted five potatoes (one small potato, four big ones) and three onions and two setts.  D, F and I made a maggotory.  We also found two red magpillers - a combination of maggot and caterpillars.  We found them all in bad acorns.  Before lunch we went to the stream.  Dad found lots of crabs - none as big as the one D, F and I found.  There was a little purple vicious one.  While I was darling it and shoving my finger in his face, he bit me and I screamed.  D, F and I went somewhere else and cleared a small stream from weed and polluted the clear water.  We did it just for fun.  We also cleared a pond with weed, fish and frogs in it.  We found a huge black crab, and a tiny one.  We went for a walk at night and saw one squeaky mouse in a tree.  They are dark creamish brown all over except their bellies, which are white.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: We drove all day.  We camped off the main road, in a desert of thistles, we drove Fred up an old river bank and just stayed there, there was a beautiful new moon.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: We drove into Mashad, and just before we got lost, a man came up and asked us where we wanted to go, we said we wanted some gas.  After we had got the gas, he took us to the famous shrine where Iman Rezah was buried, we were only allowed to drive round it.  Just as we were leaving the shrine, Fred broke down.  We managed to get him going again, he stopped once more before we parked him.  Mohamet, that was the man’s name, took us to see an old caravanserai, we went right up to the top floor, there were lots of old carpets being mended, it looked very difficult.  Then we went into a carpet shop, and looked at some of the carpets and drank chai.  There were five which we really liked, so much so that we thought we might buy some, we went away to think about it.  We went to a public bath and then stayed the night outside their house.  We had some pomegranate juice, it was a little sharp.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: D
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We drove into Rezaiyeh, we stayed in the car nearly all the time, while Dad changed money etc.  Yesterday we had a blow out, so we had to go and have the tyre mended.  We met a student who spoke English, but unfortunately, he had a very bad stutter so it was difficult understanding him.  We went to see his ‘Garden’, it turned out to be a farm, 5000m2 big.  It grew apples, peaches, grapes, melons and a few vegetables.  We saw some sugar beet growing.  We bought two baskets of fruit, one of peaches, one of apples.  Then we took the mahomet back and drove to find our campsite by the lake.  We eventually found an official ‘Camping’ but everything was locked, and all the water had been turned off.  There was another van there, so we just drove onto the salt/sand and stayed there.  It stank because of all the salt, the lake was 25% salt.  There was lots of ‘sludge’ (green sludge) it was revolting, the other campers were very nice though.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: G/M
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: Right rear tyre no longer mendable therefore abandoned.  Tube mended and new tyre put on.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: We drove into Mashad, and just before we got lost, a man came up and asked us where we wanted to go, we said we wanted some gas. We managed to get him going again, he stopped once more before we parked him. We had some pomegranate juice, it was a little sharp.

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: We see lots of camels in the country.

camel.speaker: F
camel.excerpt: We went to some carvings.  There were two of hunting scenes and were very realistic.  There were elephants chasing wild boars and a man in a boat shooting them with arrows then some elephants carrying dead boars and on another wall there were people on horseback shooting stags.  They were being followed by elephants.  In one corner there were some camels in a train.  Also there was a much bigger horse with a knight in chainmail on.  It was very very realistic but bigger than lifesize and worn by weather and hands.  Also one leg was missing.  (pic - see 22 Sept - Taq-i-Boston ticket)

camel.speaker: H
camel.excerpt: We have arrived in Mashad and gone to a carpet shop with our new friend.  It is on the top floor of an old caravanserai.  We were shown lots of carpets.  Out of them we loved 4 carpets - one had camel wool and sheep's wool.

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: In the morning we went back to the carpet shop, and at last, bought 3 carpets, we bought a prayer rug, made with sheep and camel wool, a ‘flying carpet’ and a beautiful new carpet.  They were about £500 for all of them.  They were all made by nomad girls, and the dyes were all natural.

camel.speaker: F
camel.excerpt: We went to the Persian carpet shop.  It was in a caravanserai.  The carpets I liked best were a flying carpet and a praying carpet.  The prayer carpet had a bit for the body, you knelt there; two places to put your hands and a place to put your head; they had camel hair on, the rest was dyed wool (pic).  There was a man repairing a carpet.  He let me have a go but I did it wrong.  The carpet was on a loom.  The man was knotting, he used a hook knife thing to help.

camel.speaker: H
camel.excerpt: We went back to the carpet shop and had a bit of a gossip and Francis and I had about twelve lumps of sugar each.  Then, looking over the railing, we saw some wool which we went to feel, beside it was a sack of camel hair.  When we came back, we saw a man repairing a carpet on a loom, he knotted it, he tried to teach Francis, but he could not do it.  Then we went back and found Mum and Dad buying the carpets - the flying carpet, the new carpet, and the camel hair prayer carpet.  (Pic).

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: We drove out of Mashad to an old Saffand dam, it was absolutely enormous.  We walked across it, and along the river to an old tower, it went down into the ground, as well as up.  It was very cold, and starting to rain, so we decided to ford the river, instead of going all the way back to the dam.  It was only 8 inches deep at the most.  We spent the night there and it rained and rained and rained.  We left in the morning, and drove to the Iranian border, it was quite foggy and rainy.  We saw a very funny group of camels.  We left Iran with very little trouble, went on 10km through no-man’s land to the Afghan border, they were much fussier and took a long time, so I cooked some tortellini, while Mum & Dad were away.  They took 2½ hours.  The bank has shut and we needed money for the tolls, before we got to Herat, so we spent the night near the customs.  We met a man who was bicycling to Australia and invited him to have coffee, we talked to him, he was very interesting.

camel.speaker: F
camel.excerpt: It had been raining all night.  When we got up, a cold wind made everything freezing outside, so we stayed inside but did not have breakfast because we hadn’t got any bread.  We saw lots of camels.  It got warmer til we were hot.

bazaar.speaker: G/M
bazaar.excerpt: Mileage = 33003 (5403 miles travelled).  Helped some Kurds.  Sanandaj Bazaar.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We stayed the night surrounded by corn stubble fields, some super flockes passed by, but they didn’t trouble us at all.  In the morning we drove on to Sanadaj, on the way we stopped and lent some kurdish people from a Landrover, our jack.  The women were wearing super costumes (not choudas) and Mum took a picture of them.  When we arrived at Sanadaj, we found the bazaar and walked round, it was very unimpressive.  There were lots of trinkets, but nothing old, or of good quality.  There were also lots of material shops, and people were buying new clothes or material to make into clothes, for the big feast on Saturday.  We looked for a ‘Hamman’ (bath-house) but without any success.  I read ‘The House of Elrig’ by Gavin Maxwell, it was an interesting book.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: We were driving to Sanandaj, when some Kurds in a Landrover stopped us and asked for a jack.  The women all wore very pretty clothes.  Then we went to Sanandaj.  At the bazaar, I got a bulb for Dad.  It was 6 volt for the big torch, then we went to a bakery.  They got a bit of sticky dough and made a ball of it.  Then someone rolled it out flat and then someone else stuck it on the roof of an oil-lit oven.  One person got about 20 loaves, they were flat and oval.  We got 5 loaves, they were crispy.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We stayed the night just off the main road, going through some mountains, and in the morning drove off to Hamadan.  When we arrived, we found the bazaar and we went to a shop selling material for a ‘chouda’ for me, after a lot of sign language we eventually found some material that we liked and that there was enough of, the man explained that we needed 5 metres!  There were some ladies there and women customers, they and Mum draped it round me, so that we could see the general idea.  It was 450 rials (£3.60) for the 5m.  The pattern was just a little bigger than this and the blue was white, the white was blue, it was thin cotton, but not as thin and see-through as some of the other material.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: We went to Hamadan.  At a bazaar the girls got some material for a chowdah (sic).  It was blue with white patterns on.  We also got six kilos of dates.  They were delicious.  Some people were making things out of copper.  They made huge plates.  I thought they would make super pizza plates.

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: We went to the bazaar in Hamadan.  Mum bought a big box of dates which contained 6kg.  We went to a sort of restaurant and had liver kebab and bread and peaches and apples and dates.

bazaar.speaker: G/M
bazaar.excerpt: Visited Ali Qapu.  Royal Mosque.  Shah Abbas Hotel.  Shaking Minarets.  Bazaar.

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: We went to a Mosque which had mirrors all along the walls.  It had an onyx floor and the mirrors were little mirrors put in patterns.  Francis found some pieces of glass - a piece was green and diamond shape and others.  We also went to a palace and gardens.  I wore my new skirt and things which I had bought in the bazaar.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We went to the Bazaar with Pariwash, and bought Helena a costume, it was the kind that the Quash-Quai women wear, it was very see through and glittery.  In the afternoon, we went to see the girls, we picked Ali up, and then drove to the telephone factory to collect the girls.  We walked through gardens with them, and had our picture taken with them, and ate grilled corn with them.  We had Chelo(?)-Kebab for lunch.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We went to see some more tombs (3), with Pariwash.  The big gold and silver tombs, were each in a little mosque like building.  One had a museum which had a big old Clock and Bell from London on it.  It also had pottery, and many old ‘Korans’ (the Muslim Bible).  Mum, Pariwash and I had to wear chaudas, and everyone had to take off their shoes, as people prayed, and gave offerings there.  Then we went back and had lunch, packed and went.  We were sorry to go, and they wanted us to stay longer, but we had to go.  We had one last look at the bazaar and found a carrot juice place, we had some and it was very good.  Then we drove out of Shiraz dropped in at Persopolis, and then went on towards Isfahan.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: When we woke up, we saw lots of boys going to school.  I wasn’t feeling very well so I didn’t have breakfast.  We drove to the ‘Friday Mosque’, it was surrounded by a small bazaar.  It was a courtyard with IWANS on all sides, and corridors with arches ran right the way round.  It had some beautiful tiles, but was unfortunately in very bad condition.  I was wearing my chouda, and a man asked F&H if I had changed my religion!  We had lunch by the river, and played a Turkish version of Bridge.  We had Chai there.  Then we went to see the ‘Palace of Forty Columns’.  It only had 20 columns, but by looking into the pool at the front, you saw 20 more reflected.  The others went to the bazaar but I was too tired and ill.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: We went to the Friday Mosque.  It was surrounded by bazaar.  (pic) In the bazaar we found the chap who sold us the helmet.  He told us that he and his brother owned two shops.  They chanted every now and then.  The mosque was made by lots of people.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We slept by the park again.  We went to see the ‘Shah Loftalla Mosque’.  It was very beautiful.  Then we walked on to the Bazaar, F&H bought a shield and an axe, Mum & Dad paid for the shield.  I bought a hand-painted necklace, and Mum & Dad bought me some matching earrings.  In the afternoon, we went to a very good bookshop, we bought lots of books, we spent £10.  We got two Bible books and some books about Iran, we also got some fiction books.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: We went to the Shiek Lofteller Mosque.  The entrance was a small dark passage leading to a dome.  There were lots of paintings but not in bright colours.  Then we went to the bazaar.  Mum and Dad brought me and H a shield - a big one with knobs on it.  The handle was loose leather fixed in four places.  Helena and I brought an axe (pic).  It had two blades and a spike.  There were dents in the axe handle.  Denise got a necklace and some earrings.

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: We went to the bazaar at one shop (the only one I can remember) Denise bought a necklace of three crescents with silver things dangling from them.  I bought a mirror which looks like this. (Pic)

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: Isfahan is full of lots of little bazaars.  I liked the brass best - especially the chainmail.  The shop I liked best was quite big and had three floors.  One room had a pile of helmets in a corner.  They had chainmail at the back.  In another room there was a pile of shields.

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: Isfahan Bazaar is really super, (I think), especially the brass section.  There is one shop that Francis and I like best and it has helmets, shields, axes and necklaces.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: At 8.00pm we drove to the Shah Abbas Hotel, to pick up Mogados(?).  We drove to the bazaar, everyone except Francis bought shoes.  Mum and Dad bought a nice copper jug.  I bought a mirror with doors, it had a crack, so I got it very cheap.  I also bought a mascara brass jar.

mosque.speaker: G/M
mosque.excerpt: Visited Ali Qapu.  Royal Mosque.  Shah Abbas Hotel.  Shaking Minarets.  Bazaar.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: Stayed the night in a campsite, nice pool, the rest not very good.  In the morning, we went to the ‘Kings Square’ we saw the ‘Ali Quapu’ and the ‘Masjid Shah’ (Shah Mosque) they were both very beautiful.  We went to see the ‘Shah Abbas’ Hotel (De-Luxe).  We had met someone last night, who was a bell-boy there, and he showed us round, it was very luxurious, and had some beautiful Persian art.  It was built on an old caravanserai, it was rooms built all round a big garden with a main bit at the front.  Then Moghers(?) showed us round the ‘Shaking Minaret’ and then we went to his house, and ate.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: We went to Ali Qabu - it was where the Shah used to get entertainment - and watched people playing polo.  It had tiles - not mosaics - because Shah Abbas the great was afraid that he might die before it was finished.  He did in fact die before it was finished.  The tiles were beautiful.  Some of them had gold on them.  Ones I liked most were of some animals and birds running wild.  There were lots of different animals.  I liked the snow cats best.  We took some photos then we went to the Royal Mosque.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: We drove into Shiraz and went to see Ali (one of the students) he showed us a tomb, it was like a mosque, it had mosaics of little ?? some were coloured.  Then we saw a palace, it was beautiful.  Then we went to Pariwash’s house.  We had an enormous Iranian lunch, it was delicious, they had a man servant, he was very sweet and old.  We went to see the tombs of Saadi and Hafez (both poets).  They were surrounded by beautiful gardens.

mosque.speaker: H
mosque.excerpt: We went to a Mosque which had mirrors all along the walls.  It had an onyx floor and the mirrors were little mirrors put in patterns.  Francis found some pieces of glass - a piece was green and diamond shape and others.  We also went to a palace and gardens.  I wore my new skirt and things which I had bought in the bazaar.

mosque.excerpt: We went to the Friday Mosque and on the way back we met our friend in his other shop.  (He owns two shops).  In that shop of general interest there were belts and neck-protectors.

mosque.excerpt: We slept by the park again.  We went to see the ‘Shah Loftalla Mosque’.  It was very beautiful. mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: We slept in the park again, when I woke up, I felt a little better, so I had some cereals for breakfast.  After breakfast I didn’t feel so well again though.  A little girl watched us having breakfast, and while we were ‘doing things’ to the van she bought her little brother/sister, s/he was very sweet, I took a photo of them.  We went to see a nice garden it was surrounded by a beautiful mosque.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: The mosques had lots of blue in.  I didn’t like them much.  I don’t know why.  Probably because they were too quiet for me.

mosque.speaker: H
mosque.excerpt: I did not like any of the mosques.  In the evening, Francis and I climbed a mountain and found lots of walls and the place where a fire had been.  We carried over about ten big rocks.

mosque.speaker: H
mosque.excerpt: I did not like any of the mosques but one room in the Shah’s entertaining house.  In the evening, F and I climbed a mountain and built a wall.  We saw the moon rising.  It rose very fast.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: We woke up very early (6.00), got dressed and set off, Ibex hunting.  We passed a dead fox on the road, it had been run over.  We scanned the mountains but couldn’t see a thing.  We drove on and made a detour to a little mosque, there was a pool in front of it, fed by mineral springs, there were lots and lots of carp (fish) in it.  Dad went swimming, he touched a fish.  He now has a cold.  Mum will show him no sympathy.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: We went to a mosque.  It had a mineral water spring but was not hot.  They had made the water flow into a pool.  The pool was full of litter and huge carps.  Dad went and had a swim.  He touched a carp - 15 inches.  Before we went to bed we wrote lots of letters so that we could post them at Mashad.

carpet.excerpt: We went to Mashad.  A nice man met us, he had a Honda and took us to a carpet shop.

carpet.excerpt: We have arrived in Mashad and gone to a carpet shop with our new friend.  It is on the top floor of an old caravanserai.  We were shown lots of carpets.  Out of them we loved 4 carpets - one had camel wool and sheep's wool.

We had some pomegranate juice, it was a little sharp.

caravanserai.speaker: H
caravanserai.excerpt: We have arrived in Mashad and gone to a carpet shop with our new friend.  It is on the top floor of an old caravanserai.  We were shown lots of carpets.  Out of them we loved 4 carpets - one had camel wool and sheep's wool.

caravanserai.speaker: F
caravanserai.excerpt: We went to the Persian carpet shop.  It was in a caravanserai.  The carpets I liked best were a flying carpet and a praying carpet.  The prayer carpet had a bit for the body, you knelt there; two places to put your hands and a place to put your head; they had camel hair on, the rest was dyed wool (pic).  There was a man repairing a carpet.  He let me have a go but I did it wrong.  The carpet was on a loom.  The man was knotting, he used a hook knife thing to help.

chai.speaker: D
chai.excerpt: When we woke up, we saw lots of boys going to school.  I wasn’t feeling very well so I didn’t have breakfast.  We drove to the ‘Friday Mosque’, it was surrounded by a small bazaar.  It was a courtyard with IWANS on all sides, and corridors with arches ran right the way round.  It had some beautiful tiles, but was unfortunately in very bad condition.  I was wearing my chouda, and a man asked F&H if I had changed my religion!  We had lunch by the river, and played a Turkish version of Bridge.  We had Chai there.  Then we went to see the ‘Palace of Forty Columns’.  It only had 20 columns, but by looking into the pool at the front, you saw 20 more reflected.  The others went to the bazaar but I was too tired and ill.

chai.speaker: D
chai.excerpt: We drove into Mashad, and just before we got lost, a man came up and asked us where we wanted to go, we said we wanted some gas.  After we had got the gas, he took us to the famous shrine where Iman Rezah was buried, we were only allowed to drive round it.  Just as we were leaving the shrine, Fred broke down.  We managed to get him going again, he stopped once more before we parked him.  Mohamet, that was the man’s name, took us to see an old caravanserai, we went right up to the top floor, there were lots of old carpets being mended, it looked very difficult.  Then we went into a carpet shop, and looked at some of the carpets and drank chai.  There were five which we really liked, so much so that we thought we might buy some, we went away to think about it.  We went to a public bath and then stayed the night outside their house.  We had some pomegranate juice, it was a little sharp.

ibex.speaker: D
ibex.excerpt: When F, H & I woke up, Mum and Dad weren’t in the van.  When they came back, they said that they had been looking for Ibex and had seen some, far away.  We all got dressed and had breakfast, and then F, H & I went exploring.  We found a big crab in a stream, we followed the path by the stream and came to a very very high waterfall (about 40/50 feet high, only a foot wide though) it made a pool, and the stream tumbled out of it.  We found some barbeque places and had lunch at one of them. While collecting firewood, I saw the carcass of a wild boar. We had fried banana, ham and jacket potatoes.  Later on, we were playing with crabs and Helena was holding one and saying ‘oh my little darling’ etc, when suddenly it pinched he and she really screamed, it was funny!  Later on we de-polluted another stream.  We also made a maggotery, we got them from bad acorns. [the maggots]

ibex.speaker: F
ibex.excerpt: We woke up at seven.  Mum and Dad weren’t there.  They had been looking for ibex.  They saw some but very far away.  H, D and I went to explore a path.  It led to a big waterfall.  I saw a big crab, it was about an inch long and much wider.  We took Mum and Dad there.  We found other ones, smaller than our one (smallest was purple and very vicious).  Helena was picking it up and saying ‘oh my darling’ etc when it pinched her.  She screamed.  (pic)

ibex.speaker: D
ibex.excerpt: We woke up very early (6.00), got dressed and set off, Ibex hunting.  We passed a dead fox on the road, it had been run over.  We scanned the mountains but couldn’t see a thing.  We drove on and made a detour to a little mosque, there was a pool in front of it, fed by mineral springs, there were lots and lots of carp (fish) in it.  Dad went swimming, he touched a fish.  He now has a cold.  Mum will show him no sympathy.

crab.speaker: H
crab.excerpt: Golegosten Park.  Francis, Dad, Denise, Mum and I had lunch.  Dad made a fire in a metal thing with holes in the bottom and sides and half of it was strips of metal forming a grill.  We fried four small bananas, eight slices of ham, roasted five potatoes (one small potato, four big ones) and three onions and two setts.  D, F and I made a maggotory.  We also found two red magpillers - a combination of maggot and caterpillars.  We found them all in bad acorns.  Before lunch we went to the stream.  Dad found lots of crabs - none as big as the one D, F and I found.  There was a little purple vicious one.  While I was darling it and shoving my finger in his face, he bit me and I screamed.  D, F and I went somewhere else and cleared a small stream from weed and polluted the clear water.  We did it just for fun.  We also cleared a pond with weed, fish and frogs in it.  We found a huge black crab, and a tiny one.  We went for a walk at night and saw one squeaky mouse in a tree.  They are dark creamish brown all over except their bellies, which are white.
